text:
Corridor #4- begins from an interchange location at existing I-94 but would be located north and west of the airport in the vicinity of South 6th Street. A freeway access interchange to I-94 in this location would be 1/2 mile south of the Howard Avenue interchange and one mile east of the directional interchange at Layton Avenue. The motorist traveling on I-94, oriented to the airport, would be hindered by the short weaving movements between these two interchanges. The design geometrics of interchange ramps would be further complicated with the requirement of bridge separations over 6th Street.
An interchange in this area would be disruptive to the subdivisions and mobile homes adjacent to I-94. The southwest interchange ramp would be disruptive to a large industrial complex.
Between Bolivar and Layton Avenue the corridor would disrupt an existing neighborhood by serving the highly developed subdivision. The subdivision consists primarily of single family residential units.
From the I-94 interchange this corridor extends southerly along the elevated lands of the abandoned rights of way of the North Shore Railroad located between 5th and 6th Streets. Just north of Layton Avenue the corridor would occupy the vacant 2 acre City of Milwaukee School property. South of Layton the corridor would be disruptive to a highly developed industrial area and would sever the western portion of the Airport Industrial Park located north of Edgerton Avenue.
This corridor crosses the concrete open channel sections of the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage Commission drainage system at two locations south of Layton and Edgerton Avenues.
